This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It ends
with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. The full explanations,
examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary game-loop frame-rate coordinate-system origin axis coordinate ordered-pair quadrant handedness >}}

## 1.1 Mathematics in game development

- For a computer, a game is numbers in memory: positions, health, score.
- The **game loop** repeats: read the input → change the numbers → draw.
- One pass makes one **frame**.
- **Frame rate**: frames per second (fps). Phone games: 30 or 60 fps.
- At 60 fps, the loop runs 60 times every second.
- The mathematics of this course in a game:

| What the game does | Mathematics |
|---|---|
| know where every object is; move it | coordinates, vectors |
| aim a turret; make an object bob up and down | trigonometry |
| move, turn and resize models | matrices |
| decide if a door opens or an enemy attacks | logic |
| loot, critical hits, random levels | probability |

![The game loop.](images/game-loop.png){width=70%}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Find the mathematics in a game"}
Play a game on your phone for two minutes. Write four things it must compute
with numbers (for example "the position of my car"). Next to each, write the
mathematics it needs.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · The game loop"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="draw first|vectors|60 frames"}
The loop has read the player's tap. What does it do next?
:   change the numbers

A game runs at 60 fps. How many frames in 10 seconds?
:   600 frames

What does one pass of the game loop make?
:   one frame

A turret must turn to aim at a ship. Which mathematics?
:   trigonometry

A ship drops a rare reward only sometimes. Which mathematics?
:   probability
:::
:::

## 1.2 One-dimensional coordinates

- A **number line** has an **origin** (0), a unit and a positive direction.
- A point has one number: its **coordinate**. Left of 0: negative.
- A runner game needs one number for the position.
- A board game uses **whole numbers** (square 3, never 3.5). A running game
  can also use **decimal numbers** (3.5).
- **Displacement** = end − start. Plus: right (or up). Minus: left (or down).
- **Distance** = the displacement without the sign. Never negative.

![A runner game: the player goes back from 4 to the checkpoint at −3.](images/number-line.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A distance is never negative. −7 is a displacement; its distance is 7.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · A runner track on paper"}
Draw a number line from −5 to 10. Mark the start at 0, a coin at 6 and a trap
at −2. The player runs to the coin, then falls back to the trap. Write the
displacement and the distance of each move.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Moving along a line"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="−8|decimal numbers"}
The player goes from 4 back to the checkpoint at −3. Displacement?
:   −7

The distance of that move.
:   7 units

The player runs from 0 to a coin at 6. Displacement?
:   +6

A displacement of −5 and one of +5. Their distances?
:   both 5 units

A board game piece can stand only on squares 1, 2, 3… What kind of numbers?
:   whole numbers
:::
:::

## 1.3 Two-dimensional coordinates

- Two axes cross at the origin: the **x-axis** (right) and the **y-axis** (up).
- A point is an **ordered pair** (x, y). The order matters.
- Four **quadrants**: I (+, +), II (−, +), III (−, −), IV (+, −).
- A point with a 0 is on an axis, not in a quadrant.
- Moving right or left changes x; moving up or down changes y.

![The four quadrants and their signs.](images/quadrants.png){width=62%}

{{< sim file="sims/grid-strike.html" poster="sims/grid-strike.png" title="Grid Strike: hit the coordinates" kind="game" height="600" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Build the level in GeoGebra"}
Open geogebra.org/calculator (free, no account). Type `Coin = (4, 3)`,
`Key = (-3, 2)` and `Exit = (2, -3)`. Add an enemy in quadrant III and a door
on the y-axis. Then play stage 1 of **Grid Strike**.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Where is the point?"}
Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="quadrant I|quadrant IV|on the y-axis"}
The key at (−3, 2).
:   quadrant II

Both numbers of a point are negative. Which quadrant?
:   quadrant III

A tree at (−5, 0).
:   on the x-axis

A player at (2, 1) moves 3 right and 4 up. New position?
:   (5, 5)

The point 3 units right of the centre and 2 units down.
:   (3, −2)
:::
:::

## 1.4 Three-dimensional coordinates

- A third axis, **z**, at a right angle to x and y.
- A point is an **ordered triple** (x, y, z).
- In most engines y is up: y is the **height**.
- On the ground, y = 0.
- x and z say where the point is on the ground.

![The three axes of a 3D world.](images/axes-3d.png){width=60%}

{{< sim file="sims/position-3d.html" poster="images/axes-3d.png" title="Place an object in 3D" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Move a player in 3D"}
In the 3D viewer, move the player to (1, 2, 4). Which slider changes the
height? Then catch three coins and write their coordinates.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Positions in 3D"}
In these questions, y is up. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="−3 units|(4, 12, 0)"}
A drone at (4, 12, −3). How high is it?
:   12 units

A box at (5, 0, 5). Where is it?
:   on the ground

A tower on the ground at x = 4, z = −3. Its position?
:   (4, 0, −3)

The drone lands straight down. Which number changes?
:   only y

A at (1, 4, 2), C at (3, 7, −1). Which is higher?
:   C
:::
:::

## 1.5 Left-handed and right-handed systems

- With x right and y up, z can point **into** or **out of** the screen.
- Hand rule: thumb +x, index finger +y, middle finger +z.
- Works with the left hand: **left-handed** (+z into the screen).
- Works with the right hand: **right-handed** (+z towards you).
- Unity: y up, left-handed. Blender: z up, right-handed.
- Different up axes: a model from Blender can appear lying on its side in
  Unity, so always check which axis is up.

![Left-handed and right-handed coordinate systems.](images/handedness.png){width=86%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Not all 3D programs use the same axes. Check which axis is up before you read
a position.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The hand rule"}
Hold your left hand in front of the screen: thumb right, index finger up.
Where does your middle finger point? Do the same with your right hand. Which
hand fits Unity?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Which hand?"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="down|x"}
Left hand: thumb right, index finger up. Where does +z point?
:   into the screen

The handedness of Unity.
:   left-handed

The handedness of Blender.
:   right-handed

The up axis in Blender.
:   z

A Blender model appears lying on its side in Unity. Why?
:   the up axis is different
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Harbor Guard {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Harbor Guard** is a tower-defence game for phones. It runs at 60 fps. The
origin of the harbour level is in its centre: the dock is at (0, −6), the
lighthouse at (−4, 5) and the gate at (3, 2). A ship enters at (5, 8) and
sails to the dock. In the 3D version, a drone flies at (4, 12, −3) with y up,
and the towers are made in Blender, where z is up.

{{< sim file="sims/harbor-guard.html" poster="sims/harbor-guard.png" title="Harbor Guard: build towers at the right coordinates" kind="game" height="720" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · The harbour (harder)"}
Harbor Guard: 60 fps; dock (0, −6), lighthouse (−4, 5); a ship enters at
(5, 8); drone (4, 12, −3) with y up; towers made in Blender (z up). Choose the
right answer.

::: {.match extra="quadrant I|on the x-axis|60 frames"}
How many frames does the game make in 5 seconds?
:   300 frames

The lighthouse at (−4, 5). Quadrant?
:   quadrant II

The dock at (0, −6). Where is it?
:   on the y-axis

The ship sails from y = 8 down to y = −6. Displacement in y?
:   −14

How high is the drone?
:   12 units

In Blender, which number of a tower's position is its height?
:   the last number
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- The game loop: read → change → draw, once per frame.
- On a line: displacement = end − start; distance has no sign.
- (x, y): four quadrants, decided by the signs.
- (x, y, z): with y up, y is the height and the ground is y = 0.
- Hand rule: Unity is left-handed (y up), Blender right-handed (z up).
